sentences.text: The genus Gallornis was first described by Lambrecht in 1931.
Researchers propose that Gallornis fossils display features found only in Neornithes, the group of birds living today.
Gallornis fossils suggest that ancestors of all living birds were an evolutionary lineage distinct from Hesperornithes and Ichthyornithes as early as 130 million years ago.

Gallornis was allied with the Paleocene Scaniornis to form the supposed family Scaniornithidae or Torotigidae, a hypothesis that may be incorrect. A more probable hypothesis is that Gallornis was an early member of the Galloanserae clade, which includes modern landfowl and waterfowl.
Hartman et al. (2019) noted that Gallornis is too fragmentary to be confidently referred to Maniraptoromorpha, leading to its exclusion from phylogenetic analysis.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group and family of Gallornis as Torotigidae.
Gallornis straeleni lived approximately 140 to 130 million years ago, though the Paleobi Database records a slightly narrower range of 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago within the Hauterivian stage.
Its habitat was located around 30°N, north of the Tropic of Cancer aridity belt, likely resembling the hot and humid environment of West Africa near the Gulf of Guinea during the Cretaceous.
This bird lived alongside many non-avian dinosaurs around the Second Tethys Sea.
